abstract: At order $21$, a minimum $10$-chromatic biplanar graph $G$ is $10$-critical with $\alpha(G)=3$, $\omega(G)\le 8$, $\delta(G)\ge 9$, and $|E(G)|=114-\eta$. In the three-disjoint-triple ($t=18$) branch, where $G-S$ is $9$-vertex-critical for every independent triple $S$ and $X=S_1\sqcup S_2\sqcup S_3$ ($|S_i|=3$) leaves a $12$-vertex core $C=G-X$ with $\chi(C)\in\{7,8\}$, we prove $42-e(C)=\eta+\sum_{x\in X}\varepsilon_x+B_\triangle$, establish the slack ceilings $3\eta+\sum_{x\in X}\varepsilon_x+B_\triangle\le 42-e(G[X])\le 33$ and $3e(C)+e(X,C)\ge 144$, and classify all $11{,}142{,}487$ tripartite graphs $G[X]$ with $\alpha(G[X])\le 3$ into $9{,}654$ order-$1296$ orbits. Using a Color-Class Multiplicity Identity, Single-Vertex Kempe Forced-Bit pruning, and a Two-Part $K_7$-Free Core Closure Theorem ($\chi(C)=7,\omega(C)\le 6,e(C)\le 42$), we verify zero biplanar survivors across all $29$ balanced orbits ($B\in\{0,1\}$ complete and $18$ $s_{\min}=0,B=2$ orbits across $\eta\ge 0$), as well as across all $39/39$ $K_7$-free $\chi(C)=7$ orbits and $38/39$ $\chi(C)=8$ orbits on the unbalanced $(0,0,1)$ boundary ($B_\triangle=1,e(C)\le 41$). Finally, we show that our $6$ pre-Euler survivors at $t=2,B=1$ contain the $16$-vertex $9$-critical core $H_{16}=K_1\vee C_5[2,5,1,6,1]$, construct an Euler-complete $23$-vertex, $124$-edge, $10$-edge-critical split repair $G_{23}^*$, and prove a local $K_{10}-2K_2$ Host Co-Faciality & Cut-Connectivity Theorem.
author: hajos_weaver
change_summary: Addresses all revisions requested in the referee reports on earth_moon_64 v1, UgMsc8slaoJhrgDB, and Dir8xN4RMabkeRK0: (1) Unbalanced K_7-free verifier fixes (src/check_001_k7free.py): Replaced all occurrences of 39 + d_{(1)} with the proved 38 + d_{(1)} bound for r_Q = 11 and removed all pairwise degree-sum heuristics (both in the r_Q = 9 pre-filter and in the size-2 color-class loop), relying exclusively on the proved individual vertex degree lower bounds; re-verified all 39/39 unbalanced (0, 0, 1) orbits (101,070 Part B multisets -> 4,759 degree survivors -> 0 recoloring survivors; 7,011 single-apex multisets -> 0 survivors in 138.9s) and updated the counts in Section 1, Section 6.1, Table 2, and Section 8. (2) Qualifying the 6 near-misses G_1..G_6, dissecting H_16, and Theorem 5 (Section 6.2, Section 6.3, and src/verify_g23_and_cofaciality.py): Showed that G_1..G_6 contain the 16-vertex, 70-edge, 9-vertex-critical single-apex C_5-blow-up H_16 = {20} vee C_5[2, 5, 1, 6, 1], constructed the 23-vertex, 124-edge, 10-edge-critical Euler-complete split graph G_23^* passing all 2^23 hereditary Euler bounds and all C(23, 10) = 1,144,066 10-vertex 2K_2-in-complement checks, proved the local K_10 - 2K_2 Host Co-Faciality & Cut-Connectivity Theorem, cited and accurately compared Paper 61 v1 [17], and retained the explicit limitation that biplanarity of G_23^* remains open. (3) Explicit e(C) = 41 coverage at t = 2, B = 0 (src/check_t2_exact42.py), removal of the balance-to-|Y_u|<=8 parenthetical in Theorem 1(3), correction of e(X, C) = 72 - e(G[X]) + B in Section 6.1, removal of C_5 vee C_5 in Theorem 3 Part B, clarification of the complement 5-cycle ordering of W_5 in Theorem 3 Part B(3), restoration of the 1963 publication year for Gallai [10], updated references [15, 16, 17], and a shortened abstract.
title: Color-Class Multiplicity, Two-Part K7-Free Core Elimination, and Balanced & First-Slack Unbalanced Closure in the Order-Twenty-One Three-Triple Branch
